app_documentation:
Simple Task Manager is a web-based personal task management application that lets individuals record, track and clean up the work they need to do in a private, secure space. It is built as a React front end backed by a Node.js and Express REST API, with JWT-based authentication and a PostgreSQL database. The design is mobile-first, with a calm indigo visual style, card-based task lists, a bottom navigation bar (Tasks, New Task, Account) and touch targets of at least 44px. It centers on a persistent quick-add field and status filters so that common actions, such as creating a task, take no more than two interactions from the main screen.

The MVP delivers five features. F1 Create Tasks (High): users add a task with a required title and an optional description of up to 500 characters, and an empty title is rejected with a validation error. F2 Complete Tasks (High): users mark tasks complete or reopen them, and the change persists after reload. F3 Delete Tasks (High): users permanently delete tasks after confirming in a dialog, and the task is removed from the list and the database. F4 View and Filter Tasks (Medium): users see only their own tasks, newest first, and can filter by All, Active or Completed. F5 User Authentication (Medium): visitors register and log in or out with email and password, so that tasks stay private. The experience spans seven screens: Login, Register, My Tasks, New Task, Task Details and Account, plus the delete confirmation dialog. Supporting UI elements include a progress summary, empty state, toast messages and an account stats card.

The intended users are individuals who need a simple, private to-do list. The defined roles are User and Administrator. Regular users can access only their own tasks, and cross-user access attempts return HTTP 403. The data model has two tables. The users table holds a uuid id, a unique lowercased email, a bcrypt password hash, a role (user or administrator) and timestamps. The tasks table holds a uuid id, a user_id foreign key with ON DELETE CASCADE, a title, an optional description, an is_completed flag, completed_at, and timestamps. A composite index on (user_id, is_completed, created_at) supports filtered, newest-first listing. Deletes are hard deletes, and timestamps are stored in UTC.

Quality targets are: task list pages load in under 2 seconds with 100 concurrent users; passwords hashed with bcrypt and all traffic served over HTTPS; 99.5% monthly uptime; task creation in two interactions or fewer; and strict per-user privacy. Accessibility follows WCAG AA contrast, with visible focus rings, ARIA labels, focus-trapped dialogs and screen-reader-announced errors. Delivery follows a 13-task MVP plan covering schema and migrations, API scaffolding, auth, task APIs (create, complete/reopen, delete, list), shared UI components, the screens, integration and load testing, and deployment with managed PostgreSQL, HTTPS and uptime monitoring. Key risks to manage are scope creep beyond the five features, JWT and ownership-check mistakes, frontend dependency on the APIs, performance and uptime on low-tier hosting, and a single-developer critical path.
baseline_artifacts: Requirements_v1 (Simple Task Manager: features F1-F5, technical and non-functional requirements, user roles)
Design_v1 (mobile-first UI design: color scheme, typography, navigation, six screens, UI component library, accessibility and responsive guidelines)
Database_v1 (PostgreSQL schema: users and tasks tables, indexes, relationships and assumptions)
CyclePlan_v1 (Simple Task Manager MVP Plan: tasks T1-T13, dependencies, estimates and risks)
SupportGovernance_v1 (app documentation, baseline register and glossary)

glossary.Task: A single to-do item owned by one user, with a required title, an optional description of up to 500 characters, and a completion status (active or completed).
glossary.JWT (JSON Web Token): A stateless, signed token issued at login and verified by API middleware to identify the authenticated user without server-side sessions.
glossary.Reopen: Returning a completed task to the active (incomplete) state, which resets is_completed to false and clears completed_at.
glossary.Ownership Check: An application-layer check that compares tasks.user_id with the authenticated user and returns HTTP 403 when a user tries to access another user's task.
glossary.Hard Delete: Permanent removal of a task record from the PostgreSQL database after user confirmation, with no soft-delete or recovery.
glossary.Baseline: A formally approved, versioned snapshot of a project artifact (for example Requirements_v1, Design_v1 or Database_v1) used as the reference point for change control and support.
